checklist: FOR WHOEVER ADDS A SYSTEM (gate 123, tools/budget-gate.ts, holds these rows; node tools/cost.ts shows where a year goes).
1. Keep its state per land, realm or world, never per person: a person is read off those numbers when someone looks (host/), not kept and stepped.

2. Run it yearly or slower, and say the cadence where it is registered (world.system's every); what moves over decades runs by the decade, at an offset so that not every slow system falls on the same year.
3. Keep faded sums, not logs: a running number with a half-life in place of a list that grows with the years. Whatever list it does keep has a stated most and drops its oldest.

4. Give it a deep-time path: its year must cost the same at year 3,000 as at 300 for the same lands and realms, and nothing in it may walk all history. Read the events of this year from the log's end, never the log whole.
5. Bound its store and give the store a byte budget here; while it holds nothing it is dormant() and hashed as if not there, so it moves no world it has had no part in.

6. Add no draws to a stream others draw from: a new system draws on a stream of its own name, so that every older history stays what it was (node tools/oracle.ts unchanged, or --expect its domain alone).

7. Loop over what is near, not over all pairs: a realm's neighbours, a land's neighbours, the realms that have met. A loop over realms times realms, or lands times towns, needs a reason written beside it.
8. Allocate nothing by the land each year that could be kept: scratch arrays are made once and filled again.

9. Register its row: run node tools/budget-gate.ts --write, and in the commit say what its share of a year is on each world below and why that is worth it. A system that takes a share over its budget, or writes more events, decisions or bytes than its row, fails the gate by name.
